meta.note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list as published by Exophase and PSNProfiles (checked 19 Nov 2026). Counts are PSN's tracked progress targets from PSNProfiles. Every guide below is written in our own words for this guide; sources are named beside each trophy. Where launch guides had not yet confirmed a method, the guide says so instead of inventing one.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is no separate task to chase: it is the finish line of the whole roadmap. Work the stages in order — story, strangers and character quests, collectibles, activities, then the 100% cleanup — and it unlocks on its own. PowerPyx rates the whole platinum about 4/10 difficulty and roughly 200 hours, long rather than hard, with no online trophies and no difficulty setting to worry about.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Automatic story trophy: finish the opening mission Gone Fishing in Chapter 1 and it unlocks. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to miss — just play the first mission through. PowerPyx lists it as automatic and unmissable, the first story trophy of the game.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission of Chapter 1 and the trophy unlocks at the chapter's end. Before you leave Chapter 1, do the one thing that cannot wait: meditate at the Chapter 1 spot for Positive Mental Attitude, which PowerPyx flags as the list's only potentially missable trophy. Keep a manual save at the start of each chapter, because GTA VI has no mission replay.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission of Chapter 2. This is the chapter where both Lucia and Jason become playable together, which opens most of the free-roam list, so use the chapter to start side content between missions rather than rushing straight through. Make a manual save when the chapter starts, since there is no mission replay to fall back on.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission of Chapter 3. The robbery trophies open up in Chapters 3 and 4, so from here on, plan robberies deliberately instead of grabbing them at random: five bank vaults for Maximum Withdrawal and one illegal operation per gang for Pest Control. Save at the chapter start; there is no mission replay.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission of Chapter 4, the last chapter before the finale. Before the final mission, make a separate manual save: the finale is a natural point of no return, and a spare save lets you mop up anything left behind without replaying the story. PowerPyx notes the final mission trophy itself is automatic once you finish it.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: One of only two gold trophies: finish the final story mission after Chapter 4 and it unlocks. It is automatic and cannot be missed by playing the story, so the only preparation is the manual save recommended before the finale. After the credits, the whole map stays open for the collectible, activity and 100% stages.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run when it appears in your mission list. Like the other named-mission trophies it unlocks automatically on completion, so follow the mission objectives as given and it pops at the end. There is no mission replay in GTA VI, so a manual save before the mission is cheap insurance if you want to redo it.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. It is a named story heist, so it unlocks automatically when the mission ends; play it as part of the story and do not skip its setup steps. This is one of the big set-piece missions, so expect a longer session than a normal story mission.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Automatic on mission completion, like the other named-mission trophies — no extra objective beyond finishing the mission itself. If you are tracking the story trophies in order, this is one of the mid-story mission trophies between the chapter trophies.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. It unlocks automatically at the end of the mission, so there is no hidden objective to hunt for. The name is a story spoiler in itself, which is why this guide's spoiler setting hides it until you earn it.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown at the airport. Automatic on completion. Note the related free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can also happens at VCIA — an unscheduled departure — so once the story mission is done, remember the airport as a spot for that separate trophy rather than trying to force it during the mission.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Automatic on completion, as with the other named story missions. The mission name suggests a heavy combat sequence, so stock up on armour and ammo before starting it rather than mid-mission, and keep a manual save from before the mission.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: The second gold and the hardest trophy on the list: reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist (Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion, which appears after the story). PowerPyx stresses the checklist is lenient — roughly 60% of true completion, not everything — and most side quests are not required, while collectibles count only partly. Both PowerPyx and the EGamers roundup rank it the hardest trophy; save it for the final cleanup stage and let every other stage feed into it.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete any 250 of the 397 stunts across Leonida: 130 stunt jumps, 202 under-the-bridge flights, 40 knife flights between buildings and 25 base jumps, per PowerPyx. You do not need all 397, and the 100% checklist asks for 300, so the trophy lands on the way to the full requirement. Mix stunt types as you travel instead of grinding one type, and check the in-game stunt tracker as you go.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample all 9 activity types at least once — PSN tracks 0/9. The fastest way is to treat it as a sampler tour early on: one race, one fishing trip, one arcade game, one shooting-range visit, one drone race, one bowling game, one meditation, one stunt and one more activity from the list. It pairs naturally with the activity stage, and trying everything once also tells you which activities you enjoy grinding later.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Take gold in all 42 shooting-range challenges — PSN tracks 0/42. Treat each challenge as a short drill: learn its scoring first with a bronze run, then chase gold once you know the target layout. Use the range's own practice flow rather than free-roam shooting, since only range challenges count. This is one of the six silvers and a pure skill grind, so spread it across sessions instead of forcing it in one sitting.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — PSN tracks 0/14. Drone races are a distinct activity from car races, so do not expect road-racing skill to transfer directly: learn each course's turns first, then race to win. Visit a new location whenever you pass one during the collectible stage, so the wins accumulate instead of becoming a late grind.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — PSN tracks 0/20, and each race counts once, so repeating the same easy race does not help. Work through the race list across Leonida instead: different routes, different vehicle classes, different starting points. Shorter sprint races are the efficient picks for the count, while longer ones are worth doing for the driving practice.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Challenge Cal to a fishing contest and beat him. Fishing is one of the game's calm side activities, so the challenge is more about patience than reflexes: follow the fishing prompts carefully and do not rush the reel. Do it during the strangers and side-content stage, since Cal is a side character rather than a story mission giver.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Find an arcade cabinet and finish one full arcade game. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest or the one you already understand and play it to its end screen. Arcades sit in the world as ambient activities — check entertainment spots in Vice City while you are there for other trophies, and this pops quickly.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand through to its final mission. Character quest lines like Andy's unlock as you meet them in free roam, so keep an eye out for his marker between story missions rather than only after the finale. Complete the strand's missions in order; the trophy pops at the end of the last one.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's mission strand through to its final mission. Like the other character quest lines, it runs alongside the story in free roam, so pick up Kenton's missions as they appear instead of leaving the whole strand for after the credits. The trophy unlocks when the final mission of his strand ends.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand through to its final mission. Billy's strand is one of five character quest lines with a final-mission trophy, so treat it the same way: follow its marker when it appears, finish each mission in order, and the trophy pops at the end. Doing the strands during the story keeps the post-game cleanup short.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida — PSN tracks 0/8, and it is one of the six silvers. Stranger missions appear as you explore, so the practical approach is to stop for every stranger marker you pass while doing collectibles and travel, rather than hunting all eight in one sweep. Each strand is several missions long, so start them early and finish them as their markers appear.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's mission strand through to its final mission. Randy is one of the five character quest givers with a final-mission trophy, so follow his strand's missions in order as they appear in free roam. Like the other strands, it is safest to work on it during the story, when you are travelling the map anyway.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand through to its final mission. It is the last of the five character quest lines, and the same approach applies: take his missions as they appear, finish them in order, and the trophy pops at the strand's end. With all five character strands done, the strangers stage of the roadmap is complete.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: THE missable trophy — the only one PowerPyx, GTABase and Output Lag all flag. There are 18 meditation spots (PSN tracks 0/18), and one is offered by Lucia on her balcony in Chapter 1, the morning after the mission Down to Earth, and it disappears after that chapter. Do that first meditation before finishing Chapter 1, keep a manual save at the chapter start, then work through the remaining 17 spots in free roam. There is no mission replay, so a missed Chapter 1 spot means a new playthrough.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Take on Bret's hunt for a unique animal and bring it down. Unique-animal hunts are tracked, deliberate outings rather than random encounters, so follow Bret's guidance to the animal's area and hunt it there instead of wandering. PowerPyx notes the 100% checklist separately asks you to study 100 of 255 animals through binoculars, so the binocular habit you build here pays off twice.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets — PSN tracks 0/3, and it is one of the six silvers. Cards are scattered across Leonida as a classic collectible hunt, so the efficient approach is a dedicated sweep with a checklist: collect as you travel during the story, then finish the remaining sets in the collectible stage. Keep count per set, since a set only counts when it is complete.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app to scan 100 locations — PSN tracks 0/100, and it is one of the six silvers. KeenGamer's guide recommends the WAiNK app for scanning unfamiliar vehicles and locations as you travel, so build the habit early: scan everything new you pass instead of saving it for a sweep. The same app also feeds Whip It Good's 100 discovered vehicles, so one scanning habit serves two trophies.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges — PSN tracks 0/50. PowerPyx's roadmap places this in the 100% stage, with 70 of 80 challenges feeding the completion checklist, so the 50 here land on the way to the bigger target. Challenges cover many systems at once, so do not grind them in isolation: play the activities you enjoy and check the challenge list between sessions to see what is close to done.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose the police and escape. The partner requirement is the key detail: do it during a two-character sequence, not solo. Break line of sight, get out of the search area and stay hidden until the stars clear — a fast car and a quiet hiding spot beat a shootout, since the trophy is about escaping, not fighting.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without the wanted level dropping between them. Plan a route of three close shops first, keep the pace up between robberies, and do not let the heat fade — the chain breaks if you lose the wanted level. A getaway car parked near the third shop makes the escape clean once the third robbery is done.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — PSN tracks 0/100. Discovery means finding and scanning new vehicle models, and PowerPyx notes the 100% checklist asks for 200 of 277 base-model vehicles scanned, so this trophy is the first third of that longer hunt. Use the WAiNK app to scan every unfamiliar vehicle you pass, and vary your routes so you meet new models instead of the same traffic.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Activate Combat Focus once and take down five enemies before it ends. The setup matters more than the aim: pick a fight with a group of enemies clustered together, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them quickly while it lasts. Do not waste the activation on a single enemy — wait for a proper firefight, such as a gang shootout, where five targets are in front of you.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: At Vice City International Airport, take a plane and leave without a scheduled flight — the trophy's joke is in its wording. Head to the airport, get to a runway aircraft and take off on your own terms. It pairs well with the story mission VCIA Takedown, which is also set at the airport: finish the mission first, then come back to the airport in free roam for this one.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Steal a Rhino military tank — that is the whole trophy, and the description's joke gives it away. PowerPyx's launch coverage and a launch-day video guide both confirm the method: take the tank and the trophy pops. Expect a heavy wanted response the moment you climb in, so plan your escape route before you grab it, not after.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store cleanly, without any detection. Stealth is the whole requirement: plan the entry, avoid cameras and sightlines, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails the condition, so abort and try again rather than fighting through it — a quiet retry is faster than a loud escape.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape each time — PSN tracks 0/5, and it is one of the six silvers. WikiGTAVI counts 8 bank vaults in the game, so you have three spare targets if one goes wrong. Treat each vault as a planned job: scout it, bring a getaway car, and escape cleanly before moving to the next, since only a completed robbery plus escape counts.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Find an armored truck on the road, rob it and escape. Armored trucks travel set routes, so watch traffic on main roads until one appears, then hit it quickly and break away before the police response builds. It is the single-truck version of the bigger robbery trophies, and a good warm-up for the five bank vaults.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Visit every area of the Leonida map — PSN tracks 0/52 locations. The practical approach is a systematic sweep by region rather than random driving: work through the map district by district and check the area counter as you go. It overlaps heavily with the collectible stage, so explore while hunting cards, meditation spots and WAiNK locations instead of doing it as a separate chore.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation for every gang — PSN tracks 0/9 gangs. WikiGTAVI counts 39 gang operations in total, so there are far more targets than the nine you need: pick one operation per gang and work through the gang list methodically. Keep a note of which gangs you have hit, since the trophy only pops when every gang has been robbed once.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, order a cocktail and enjoy the view — a quiet ambient trophy, not a mission. Launch guides list its exact unlock method as not yet confirmed, so the honest advice is simple: visit the beachfront bars on Ocean Beach, look for a cocktail interaction with a view, and try it at different times of day if it does not trigger at first. Do not trust any guide that claims a precise spot before the method is confirmed.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle out of a showroom by smashing through it — the classic GTA-style exit the description hints at. Launch guides list the exact trigger as not yet confirmed, so the practical read is: take a car inside a vehicle showroom and exit through the glass rather than the door. If it does not pop, try a different showroom or a faster exit; the method will be pinned down as launch guides update.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Visit the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl a game through to the end. Bowling is one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so this trophy and that one overlap: play a full game, follow through on your throws, and it pops. The alley is a named location, so look for it by name rather than any generic bowling spot.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A cryptic trophy whose description gives no direct instruction — launch guides had not pinned its method down at launch. The wording points to a partnership activity that wins over a crowd, so the sensible approach is to play the game's duo and public activities and watch for a crowd-reaction moment. Treat it as a discovery trophy: try the social and partnership activities first, and check updated guides before grinding anything specific.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: A choices trophy with a PSN-tracked target of 500 — the count suggests a long accumulation of decisions rather than one moment. PowerPyx and GTABase link it to the Criminal Profile, which tracks how you play, and warn that the Irredeemable profile is permanent and makes police more aggressive. Play normally, make choices as they come, and check your Criminal Profile before any long rampage; the count will climb over a full playthrough.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: A cryptic trophy whose method launch guides had not confirmed — the name suggests succeeding on a second attempt at something that failed the first time. The honest approach is to keep playing and watch for a second-chance moment: retry an activity or event you failed once and complete it on the next try. Do not chase a specific method until a guide confirms one; this is one of the trophies PowerPyx marks as not yet known.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: A cryptic trophy, unconfirmed at launch — the description reads like a reaction to something strange happening in the world. The sensible approach is to explore Leonida's odd corners and random events rather than grinding a checklist, since the trigger is likely a one-off world moment. Keep it on your discovery list during the exploration stage and check updated launch guides; do not trust a precise method that no source has confirmed.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Perform a melee drive-by that bowls enemies over — a vehicle attack using a melee weapon rather than a gun. Launch guides list the method as not yet confirmed, so the practical read is: from a moving vehicle, use a melee weapon against targets at close range and keep the speed up. Pair it with a bowling-alley visit for Let’s Go Bowling, since both sit in the same activity family, and retry in open traffic if the first attempt does not register.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts — PSN tracks 0/250000. Marked Bills come from robberies and illegal work, so this trophy grows naturally out of the robbery stage: rob, then launder the take through contacts instead of spending it dirty. Track the total in the stats screen and keep laundering between jobs; it is an economy trophy, not a single payout.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across the game's shops — PSN tracks 0/100000, and every shop counts toward the same pot. The sensible way is to spend as you play: weapons, ammo, clothes and vehicle upgrades all count, so do not hoard cash for the end. If you reach the cleanup stage short of the total, buy big-ticket items you actually want rather than junk, since the money is gone either way.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property — PSN tracks 0/8. Garages are the storage that makes the vehicle collection trophies workable, so buy them as you can afford them during the collectible stage rather than all at once at the end. Check the property listings between missions; a garage bought early also gives you somewhere safe to store rare finds for Whip It Good and On the Spot.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles through the Scooter Bros app — PSN tracks 0/10. Find vehicles you want to keep, register them in the app, and they count toward the ten. It pairs directly with the vehicle discovery of Whip It Good: scan new vehicles with WAiNK, then register the ones worth keeping, so one driving session feeds both trophies.
trophies.name: On the Spot
